lines: Solid work. It took the pressure like good stone in the right wall.
It held under strain, which is the only praise that matters.
Good gear does not boast. It simply refuses to break.
The edge held, though this chip needs grinding out.
I can see where you blocked with it more than once.
The fastening stayed tight when the rest of the gear shifted.
There is mud in every joint, but nothing important has cracked.
This dent saved the piece underneath it from taking the hit.
The grip wore smooth where you held on. I can wrap it again.
You used it hard without abusing it. There is a difference.
The weight must have pulled at your shoulder after that buckle bent.
I would trust this for another fight after a proper repair.
The padding compressed on one side and did its job.
Clean the blood from the seams before it dries there.
That scrape came from a fall, not a blade. The stone left its own pattern.
The gear carried the strain and brought you home. Good result.
One rivet is loose. Catching it now saves a much worse failure later.
The surface looks rough, but the part bearing the load is still sound.
Tell me which piece felt wrong before I decide what to replace.
Leave it in the light. I want to inspect every mark before storage.
Still unmarked. Strong things do not need to boast before the load comes.
It has not met pressure yet. That can be a blessing.
Unscarred gear is not wasted if it keeps fear smaller.
The straps settled a little, so I will tighten them before storage.
Only road dust here. A cloth will handle that.
The edge never left its cover by the look of it.
Nothing tested the joints, which is the report I prefer.
Try the fit again before you put it away for long.
The padding stayed dry, so there should be no hidden damage.
I can tell this rubbed against the pack and nothing worse.
Unused gear still matters when it gives you a safe choice.
The buckles are where I set them. You did not have to rush into it.
Keep the metal oiled even when it sees no fighting.
There is no shame in bringing protection home untouched.
The balance has not shifted at all.
I will check the seams, though I doubt the trip strained them.
Better an idle piece of armor than a fresh wound.
Put it away clean and it will be ready when the bell rings.
We learned nothing about how it handles a blow, and that is fine.
Ask me again after it has done more than wait.
